transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I'm here because I've been having some trouble at work lately. I'm an artist, and I do a lot of freelance work, which means writing artist statements, taking client notes, and having meetings. But recently, people keep telling me they can't follow what I'm trying to explain. I guess when I'm talking or writing, I start jumping around a lot... like, I'll go from talking about the textures of a piece to the budget, and then to these secret meanings I'm seeing in things. It just all comes out at once, and it's making it really hard to communicate with people.
Over this same period, have you noticed your mood feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable, along with having much more energy than usual or needing less sleep?

Yeah, I have noticed that. Um, for stretches of time, I'll feel completely lit up. It's like I'm almost unstoppable, and every idea I have for a project is just brilliant. 

But it's not always a good feeling, I guess. I can get really irritable, too. Like, if a client or a collaborator makes even a small comment, I can just snap at them. And I realize it in the moment—my reaction just feels way bigger than the situation actually warrants. So yeah, my mood has definitely been swinging up like that.

When your mood isn't unusually high, irritable, or low—during times you'd say you feel more like your normal self—do you still notice your thoughts jumping around like that or still see those hidden meanings in things?

Yeah, actually. Um, there was a quieter month recently where my mood was pretty steady. I was sleeping normally again, and I didn't have that unstoppable feeling at all. 

But... even during that time, for a few weeks, I was still experiencing some of those things. I kept hearing these comments coming from behind the shelves in my workspace. And I was still reading hidden warnings into just ordinary studio materials. So, yeah, even when my mood feels normal, that stuff was still happening.
During that month when your mood was steady, about how many weeks did you continue hearing those voices or seeing hidden meanings before they went away?

Um, I'd say it was for several weeks. Like I was saying, that was a quieter month where I was sleeping normally again and just... not feeling unstoppable at all. But even with my mood leveled out like that, I still kept hearing those comments from behind the shelves and reading hidden warnings into ordinary studio materials for... yeah, probably several weeks during that time.
Thinking back to when you first started experiencing these unusual thoughts or hearing things, about how long ago did all of this begin in total?
Um, let me think back... I'd say it's been going on for roughly 11 months in total. That's when I first started noticing the messages in my materials and hearing the voice in the studio.

Over the full 11 months, would you say your mood swings (feeling unstoppable or very irritable) have been present most of the time, or have there been more weeks like that quiet month where your mood was normal but you still had the voices and hidden meanings?

Um, looking back over this whole period... I'd say the energized, irritable, and really overproductive stretches have definitely taken up more of the year than the calmer ones. The intensity kind of rises and falls, but yeah, those mood swings have been present for the majority of the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient exhibits a concurrent major mood episode with manic features (elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, inflated self-perception of ideas) together with psychotic symptoms (disorganized/tangential speech, auditory hallucinations, delusions of hidden meanings). Critically, there was a period of at least 2 weeks (described as 'several weeks' during a mood-stable month) in which psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, delusional perception) persisted in the absence of mood symptoms, satisfying the requirement for psychotic symptoms occurring independent of mood disturbance. Additionally, mood symptoms have been present for the majority of the total 11-month illness duration, meeting the criterion that mood episode be present for a substantial portion of the illness. This combination—overlapping mood and psychotic symptoms plus a distinct period of psychosis without mood symptoms, with mood symptoms predominating overall—is diagnostic of Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type (F25.0), rather than Bipolar Disorder with psychotic features (which would not have psychosis outlasting mood symptoms) or Schizophrenia (which would require psychosis predominating independent of mood).
